summary: Text-only EmbeddingGemma 2 q4 on native onnxruntime-node without transformers.js: @huggingface/tokenizers encodes ROLES[role]+text (template wraps it <bos> … <eos>), one padded ONNX run with empty image/video/audio feature tensors [0,512], attention-masked mean pool, L2. Past TOKEN_CAPS[role]: code_query/file_doc are truncated; WINDOWED_ROLES (note_doc, note_query) are split into cap-sized windows, each re-opened with <bos> and run alone (bounded memory — attention is quadratic: a 6k-token note in one run took 18 s and ~4 GB), and the unnormalised token sums are added before L2, i.e. one token-weighted mean. That approximates the whole-text vector (cos 0.986 on the 6034-token note) because the recall gate was fit on untruncated vectors. Within the cap vectors match transformers.js to cos ≥ 0.9999991. Only the embedder worker loads it.

summary: Text-only EmbeddingGemma 2 q4 on native onnxruntime-node without transformers.js: @huggingface/tokenizers encodes ROLES[role]+text (every encode comes back wrapped [<bos>=2 … <eos>=1]), one padded ONNX run with empty image/video/audio feature tensors [0,512], attention-masked mean pool, L2. Past TOKEN_CAPS[role]: code_query/file_doc are truncated; WINDOWED_ROLES (note_doc, note_query) are split by `windows` into cap-sized windows, each re-opened with <bos> (only the last keeps <eos>), and `embed` runs them one at a time and pools the UNNORMALISED token sums with `poolSums` (one token-weighted mean, then L2). The daemon uses the same `windows` + `sumWindow` + `poolSums` to run each window as its own model-process call so queries slot in between windows; both paths give bit-identical vectors. Peak RSS is set by the longest single run and is never given back (ORT arena), which is why window length matters for memory. Module top level loads no runtime, so the daemon can import `poolSums` without loading the model; only the embedder's model child processes (hooks/embed-worker.mjs) call `loadEmbedder`.

The session is created with enableMemPattern: false: memory patterns are planned and kept per input shape, and every text length is a new shape, so off saves ~140 MB peak at the same speed with bit-identical vectors (measured 2026-11-19). InferenceSession.run blocks its JS thread for the whole run: two sessions in ONE thread make a query wait behind a backfill run (p50 ~750 ms, max ~2.6 s); one tokenizer on the main thread with each session in its own worker_thread gave query p50 48 ms / max 83 ms during backfill at ~743 MB total (probe only, not built). Fidelity: q4 vs the fp32 onnx/model.onnx is cos median 0.984 (min 0.975) on 97 real texts; a GGUF Q8_0 of the same model in node-llama-cpp reached 0.9998. summary: Text-only EmbeddingGemma 2 q4 on native onnxruntime-node without transformers.js, split in two halves that load in DIFFERENT processes since PROTOCOL 2: `loadTokenizer` (the official Rust `tokenizers` napi package, Tokenizer.fromFile(tokenizer.json); encode is ASYNC, so `plan`/`windows`/`tokens` are async) lives once in the embedder daemon, and `loadSession` (the ONNX session, `sums(rows)` = one padded run → per-row UNNORMALISED token-state sums) lives in each model process. `plan(text, role)` → {tokens, rows, windowed}: one row when ROLES[role]+text fits TOKEN_CAPS[role] or is truncated to it (code_query/file_doc), else (WINDOWED_ROLES) cap-sized windows each re-opened with <bos> (only the last keeps <eos>). `embedPlanned(plans, sums)` is the ONE pooling path (single-row plans in one batch run, windowed ones one run per window pooled with `poolSums`), shared by `loadEmbedder` (tokenizer + session in one process; tests only) and hooks/embed-worker.mjs, so every path is bit-identical — verified 2026-11-22: 1393 vectors (193 real notes, 150 real prompts × 4 roles alone and in batches of 4) byte-identical to the previous all-in-one-process JS-tokenizer code, and byte-identical through the real daemon. Why: the JS @huggingface/tokenizers cost ~300 MB footprint per process (more than the q4 session, ~85 MB loaded) and was paid by MAIN and the query lane; the Rust one is ~120 MB, paid once, same ids on 809 texts. No JS fallback (removed, dependency dropped): both natives are optionalDependencies and a machine where either won't load gets 'model unavailable' (recall falls back to BM25); `runtimeAvailable` checks both. Session facts still hold: enableMemPattern false (per-shape memory patterns; off saves ~140 MB peak, same vectors); arena off and fixed-length padding buckets were worse; peak is set by the longest single run and kept, so window length is the memory lever. Fidelity q4 vs fp32: cos median 0.984. Module top level loads no runtime (the daemon imports poolSums/loadTokenizer without loading ORT).
